import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 401

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/401](https://www.erdosproblems.com/401)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos401

/--
Is there some function $f(r)$ such that $f(r)\to \infty$ as $r\to\infty$, such that, for
infinitely many $n$, there exist $a_1,a_2$ with
$$a_1+a_2> n+f(r)\log n$$
such that $a_1!a_2! \mid n!2^n3^n\cdots p_r^n$?

It is ambiguous in [ErGr80] what the intended quantifiers are on the variables (they write 'is
it true that we can find $a_1+a_2>n+f(r)\log n$...'). Comparing to previous problems such as
[728] and [729] it seems most likely that they intended to ask the formulation in the problem
statement.

The answer is yes: Barreto and Leeham have used ChatGPT to provide a proof of the stated problem
(in fact essentially the same construction as their solution to [729]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos401.lean"]
theorem erdos_401 : answer(True) ↔
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, Tendsto f atTop atTop ∧
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (hr : 1 ≤ r),
        {n : ℕ | ∃ a₁ a₂ : ℕ, 0 < a₁ ∧ 0 < a₂ ∧
          (a₁ : ℝ) + a₂ > n + f r * Real.log n ∧
          a₁.factorial * a₂.factorial ∣
            n.factorial * (∏ i ∈ Finset.range r, Nat.nth Nat.Prime i) ^ n}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos401

reformulations.difference: The infinite set ranges over all n : ℕ without a positivity restriction, so it includes the case governed by Mathlib's convention Real.log 0 = 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every fixed f and r, the relevant set of natural numbers is infinite if and only if its restriction to n ≥ 2 is infinite: only {0,1} is removed. This equivalence remains valid under the outer existential quantifier on f and universal quantifier on r. On the restricted domain the logarithm has its ordinary meaning. The full quantified equivalence was proved as Review401.full_statement_tail_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

review.notes:
The sole declaration faithfully states the source's intended infinitely-many-n formulation. The source's negative result concerns the different all-sufficiently-large-n variant. Its current PROVED (LEAN) status agrees with answer(True), research solved, and the proof annotation.

Scratch checks verified the prime indexing, positivity of the prime product, distribution of the nth power over that product, and small factorial/divisibility cases. Requiring positive factorial arguments is harmless even if zero were otherwise permitted: replacing zero by one preserves the factorial and increases the sum; this equivalence was also proved.

The cited theorem_1 supplies the required infinitude with coefficient (9/1120)(p_{r+1}−1)/log(p_{r+1}). I proved this coefficient tends to infinity and checked the correspondence of its prime product, establishing the implication to the repository formulation. The linked file contains no sorry or custom axioms; its separate Lean 4.29.1 project was not rebuilt. All scratch proofs compiled cleanly, with only standard axioms. No repository files were edited.
